locator.section: A high-degree univariate polynomial as a low-degree multivariate polynomial
locator.quote_at_most_25_words: This establishes both recovery of evaluations and injectivity on polynomials of degree strictly below $b^c$.

findings.finding: Evaluation recovery alone does not imply formal-polynomial injectivity over a finite field when b^c may exceed q. The injectivity theorem is true, and its formal left-inverse proof is already in the Lean source.
findings.why_it_matters: A reader must distinguish polynomial functions from formal polynomials; the text makes that distinction carefully elsewhere.
findings.suggested_direction: Move the formal Dec substitution before this inference, prove Dec(Enc(p))=p monomial by monomial, and infer injectivity before evaluation. Link decode_encode and encode_injective_on; do not add b^c<q.
evidence: If q<b^c then the nonzero formal polynomial Y^q−Y vanishes on all field inputs; hence evaluation recovery alone is insufficient.
